results.text: Effects of acute NaCl, KCl and KHCO3 loads on renal electrolyte excretion in humans. 1. Potassium salts increase sodium excretion in humans. To define the role of the potassium ion in this effect, we compared the effects of equimolar single oral loads of 100 mmol of NaCl and KCl on renal electrolyte excretion in seven healthy subjects. Synergistic effects of plasma-activated water and potassium chloride on the structure, function, and digestibility of low-sodium chicken myofibrillar protein. Excessive sodium intake is a major health concern, however, reducing salt in meat products often compromises the functional quality of myofibrillar protein (MP).
